Customer Database & Sales Team Analysis

Record-Keeping & Account Management Report

Author

Data Analysis Team

Published

June 5, 2026

1 Executive Summary

This report presents the findings from a full audit of the company’s customer database. The analysis covers 2,273 verified customer records across 31 active sales representatives and 20+ regions nationwide.

ImportantThree Actions Requiring Immediate CEO Attention
  1. 441 customers (19.4% of the base) are managed by just two reps — Ian and Peter — with no backup or succession plan in place.
  2. 341 customers are assigned to a placeholder entry called “Customer Office” and have no named sales representative.
  3. Address and contact data gaps exist across the database — 9.3% of customers have no street address and 4.7% have no phone number.

3 Sales Team Analysis

3.1 Customers Per Sales Representative

Figure 1 shows the number of customers each sales representative currently manages, ranked from highest to lowest.

NoteKey Observations
  • “Customer Office” (341 customers) is a placeholder — not a real rep. These accounts are effectively unmanaged.
  • Ian (232) and Peter (209) carry the heaviest legitimate workloads, each managing roughly twice the number of customers of any other rep.
  • 5 reps manage only 1 customer each — these should be verified as active.

4 Geographic Distribution

4.1 Where Are Our Customers?

Figure 3 shows how customers are distributed across cities and states nationwide, after consolidating inconsistent location entries from the raw database.

NoteGeographic Highlights
  • Ibadan / Oyo is the dominant market with 711 customers — nearly 3× the next largest location.
  • Ogun State (236), Lagos (197), and Kaduna (158) form the next tier.
  • Southern and middle-belt states hold 70–95 customers each, suggesting broad national reach but thin coverage outside the South-West.

5 Regional Coverage by Sales Rep

Figure 4 maps which reps are active in which regions, using the top 10 locations and top 15 reps. Darker cells indicate more customers.

WarningTerritory Overlap Concerns
  • Most regions have multiple reps sharing the same territory with no clear ownership — creating confusion and duplicated effort.
  • Peter is the only rep active across 6+ regions, creating a single point of failure for the South-West.
  • Ian dominates the entire South-East corridor across 31 regions.

6 Key Account Management Risks

6.1 Risk Overview

6.2 Ian — Regional Spread

ImportantIan Risk Summary

Ian is the business’s largest rep by customer count. His portfolio spans 31 regions — the widest of any rep — with no dominant anchor region (largest region: Enugu at only 22%). If Ian left, accounts would need to be redistributed across 31 different regions simultaneously, making him the highest succession risk in the business.

6.3 Peter — Regional Spread

ImportantPeter Risk Summary

Peter manages 115 customers in Ibadan/Oyo alone — the business’s single largest market (55% of his portfolio). He is also the de facto owner of this territory. Losing Peter would mean the largest customer hub in the database loses its primary relationship manager overnight. His 13 single-customer outlier regions (including Ghana, Kaduna, Benue) are geographically incoherent and likely receiving minimal attention.
